# Compacted Summary: Chapter 1 (Complete and Final – Updated 26)

## Setting and Time
- **Season/Period**: Spring through late August, then Christmas/New Year period of the first year; now nearly three weeks into the new year (1832)
- **Primary Location**: Middlemarch and surrounding areas (Lowick, the Grange, Freshitt, Mirecombe, Salwick, Wilhaven, Quenwick, Fenmere, Bryngate, Chalky Flats, Gulton, Highbury, Cheltenham, Tipton, Yoddrell's farm, Frick, Miremere, Salmere, Riverston, Quallingham, Halsell Wood, Loamford, Brassing, Stone Court, Coldcombe, St. Peter's Place, Lowick Gate, Shrubs, Dunholt, Yorkshire, Staveton)
- **Atmospheric Details**: Baker's boy frequently late; wind off water with salt and tar smell; dog barking periodically; bees in lavender behind parsonage; gulls quarreling over fish heads; carts with turnips; threatening rain (persistent but held off); frost silvering hedges; road rutted and puddled after thaw; children chasing hoops down lane; bell for vespers ringing thinly; chalk sun on forge wall; smoke from chimneys lying flat over fields; light going early at end of August; starlit darkness; frosty air in late year
- **Secondary Characters/Background**: Ilrine Corrett ("Old Ilrine"), herbalist; Eldette Corrett, cooper; Thidrek Corrett, smith; Ridan Corrett, glazier; Jotho Corrett ("Jotho the Younger"); Aessa Hollwood, ferryman; Cotho Hollwood, mason; Halan Hollwood, shepherd; Ulvie Hollwood, weaver; Thiena Hollwood, glazier; Elnar Brackwood, weaver; Senelle Brackwood, ferryman; Jovus Brackwood ("Red Jovus"), miller born at Salmere; Madan Brackwood, scribe born in Staveton

## Main Characters

**Dorothea**
- Recently widowed; residing at Lowick Manor
- Strong admiration for Caleb Garth's work knowledge
- Hopes to improve land and build good cottages
- Final Grange encounter: Will declared best is over, would live like one who saw heaven in trance
- Mistakenly believed Will's words referred to Mrs. Lydgate; experienced certainty his conduct with Rosamond should be above suspicion
- Though thought she might be what Will cared for most, doubt overcame this; credited all to friendship and obstruction from Casaubon's codicil
- Saw Will with portfolio on road; felt pang leaving him behind; wished they could have been happy thinking of each other
- Forced to keep money under Casaubon's codicil that ought to have been Will's, causing distress
- **New Development**: Described by Bulstrode as "a woman of most munificent disposition" in possession of funds she can well spare; has destined chief part of funds to another purpose; willing to consider taking Bulstrode's place in relation to Hospital; wishes ample time to mature thoughts; has informed Bulstrode no haste necessary; setting out on journey into Yorkshire with Sir James and Lady Chettam; her decision regarding Hospital contribution will depend on conclusions about land she is to see there; decision may affect her power of contributing

**Will Ladislaw**
- Spoke impetuously at Grange about what forbidden him by own pride and honor
- Passionate love for Dorothea which he forbade himself to utter; what kept him silent was that she was forced to keep money that ought to have been his
- After parting: As carriage grew smaller, certainty had much more bitterness; had no assurance she loved him
- Still at Middlemarch despite weeks since parting; frequenting Lydgate's household; warbling continually with Rosamond (scandal spreading per Mrs. Cadwallader)
- Raffles knows connection between Will and Bulstrode but deliberately conceals this as card to play
- Father was at Boulogne very ill; mother's family engaged in "respectable thieving line"; mother (Sarah) ran away after Archie Duncan rejected her
- Rejected Bulstrode's money; stated unblemished honor and unstained birth important; recognized stain through mother; refuses "ill-gotten money"; departed with determined quickness
- Wrote brief letter to Dorothea asking permission to call at Lowick

**Caleb Garth**
- Met Bulstrode regarding stable drainage at Stone Court; peculiar man lacking curiosity about personal affairs; fond of music
- Working with railroads: measured and valued outlying piece of land at Yoddrell's farm belonging to Lowick Manor; confronted laborers preparing to interfere with railroad agents
- Decided to take Fred Vincy on as assistant with desk-work and accounts; offered eighty pounds for first year, more after
- Character: ruled absolutely only on other people's behalf; on ninety-nine points Mrs. Garth decided, but on hundredth point Caleb was immovable ruler

**Mary Garth**
- Staying at Lowick Rectory with Miss Farebrother and Mrs. Farebrother
- Told Farebrother: "I have too strong a feeling for Fred to give him up for any one else"
- Upon Fred telling her of engagement with her father, touched keenly; scolded him for not seeing Farebrother's delicate feeling
- Earnestly desired to be clear she loved Fred best; determined to watch over her affections and constancy
- Currently telling stories to children at Lowick Parsonage (Rumpelstiltskin tale); Fred seated near her, watching with admiration

**Fred Vincy**
- Age four-and-twenty; son of Mr. Vincy; rejected Church vocation; took degree
- Encountered Caleb Garth at Yoddrell's farm; accepted eighty pounds for first year, more after
- Mr. Vincy responded with profound surprise and cutting disappointment; will keep no horse for Fred
- Casually mentioned to Rosamond what he heard about Casaubon's codicil mentioning Ladislaw
- Acknowledged debt to Caleb which will never be discharged
- At Lowick Parsonage: seated near Mary during storytelling; watching her with admiration
- Billiard room incident: encountered Lydgate gambling; felt shock; old opinion of Lydgate as prig reversed; Fred's usual brightness replaced by involuntary gravity and embarrassment
- **Farebrother's Intervention and Warning**: Farebrother drew Fred aside at St. Botolph's; confessed temptation to let Fred go wrong and waste Garth's opportunity; disclosed satisfaction of Fred's affections stands in way of his own; warned Mary's affection is "conditionally bound" and liable to change; claimed another man might win "firm place in her love as well as respect" through "companionship of ready sympathy" even over longest associations; Fred seized by uncomfortable chill, dreading something said to Mary; tone changed to encouraging major key; spoke of returning to old intention and uttering warning; moment produced regenerating effect in Fred; Farebrother put out hand to imply conversation closed, dropping voice on last words

**Mr. Lydgate**
- Doctor/physician; age nine-and-twenty
- **Financial Crisis Deepening**: Debt amounts to three hundred and eighty pounds at Brassing; creditor Mr. Dover holds bill of sale on furniture
- **Gambling Incident and Aftermath**: Played at billiard-table; won repeatedly but ended by losing four to five pounds overall; felt unmixed disgust next day; carried unpleasant vision of figure made, behaving like men at Green Dragon; chewed disagreeable cud of regret; reason strangled desire to gamble but feeling remained that with assurance of luck he would have liked to gamble rather than take inevitable alternative
- **Contemplating Leaving Middlemarch**: Began familiarizing imagination with step unlike his remembered self—considering whether to carry out Rosamond's notion to quit Middlemarch without seeing beyond preface; questioned whether any man would buy his practice; against this step was obstacle that purchaser might not be quickly forthcoming and Rosamond in poor lodging would not find life to save her from gloom
- **Hesitation About Bulstrode Approach**: Had created for himself strong ideal obstacles to requesting considerable help from Bulstrode, whom he had often boasted he was totally independent of; Bulstrode's opinions he thought contemptible; motives seemed absurd mixture of contradictory impressions
- **Bulstrode's Medical Consultation and Lydgate's Opportunity**: Note from Bulstrode requested Lydgate call at Bank; Bulstrode had hypochondriacal tendency showing; lacked sleep, dwelt on it as sign of threatening insanity; wanted to consult Lydgate; moment when Bulstrode received medical opinion with comfort seemed to make communication of personal need easier than in Lydgate's contemplation beforehand
- **At Bank Consultation—Hospital Crisis**: Bulstrode announced plans to cease personal share in Hospital management due to anticipated withdrawal from Middlemarch; will withdraw support except for having supplied building expenses and contributed large sums to successful working
- **Bulstrode's Plan**: Proposes amalgamation of New Hospital with Infirmary, making New Hospital special addition to elder institution with same directing board; medical management of both to be combined; states this change will remove difficulty as to maintenance and cease division of benevolent interests
- **Bulstrode's Expressed Regret**: Admits highly valued opportunity of new and independent procedure which Lydgate has diligently employed; original plan was one he had much at heart; states providential indications demand his renunciation, which he accepts
- **Dorothea as Potential Replacement Benefactor**: Bulstrode informed Lydgate that Dorothea may be certainly counted on as willing to increase contributions; had interview with her on subject; she has informed him though she has destined chief part of funds to another purpose, willing to consider taking his place in relation to Hospital; wishes ample time to mature thoughts; Bulstrode has told her no need for haste and his own plans not yet absolute; her decision will much depend on what Lydgate can tell her; she is setting out on journey into Yorkshire with Sir James and Lady Chettam; conclusions about land she is to see may affect her power of contributing
- **Lydgate's Response**: Felt renewed hope about Hospital only made him more conscious of poisoning facts; recognized his effort after help, if made at all, must be made now and vigorously; spoke with firm intention yet unwillingly; stated highest object is profession and had identified Hospital with best use of profession; acknowledged best use not always same with monetary success; explained everything making Hospital unpopular has helped with other causes connected with professional zeal to make him unpopular as practitioner; gets chiefly patients who can't pay; spoke unwillingly as if biting objectionable leek
- **Direct Appeal for Financial Help**: Made direct statement to Bulstrode of his financial position; revealed he slipped into money difficulties with no way out unless someone who trusts him and his future will advance him sum without other security; stated had very little fortune when came to Middlemarch; has no prospects from own family; marriage expenses much greater than expected; needs thousand pounds to clear himself—to free from risk of goods sold in security of largest debt, pay other debts, and leave something to keep household beforehand with small income; stated out of question wife's father would advance such sum; mentioned position to Bulstrode as only other man who may be held to have personal connection with his prosperity or ruin
- **Bulstrode's Response**: Expressed grief though not surprise at information; regretted Lydgate's alliance with brother-in-law's family of prodigal habits, already much indebted to him for sustainment in present position; advised Lydgate instead of involving himself in further obligations and continuing doubtful struggle, should simply become bankrupt

**Mr. Farebrother (Vicar)**
- Aware Lydgate is proud man; had been playing whist to satisfy mother
- After conversation at Mr. Toller's, learned something making him watch eagerly for opportunity
- **Intervention with Fred and Mary**: Left whist-table to speak with Lydgate, disclosing Lydgate had done him service by influencing him to stop playing for money; later approached Fred at billiard-table through interruption of Lydgate's play; confessed temptation to let Fred ruin himself; disclosed satisfaction of Fred's affections stands in way of his own; warned Mary's affection is "conditionally bound"; claimed another man might win firm place through companionship of ready sympathy; overcame temptation to act selfishly; at parting with Fred, voice dropped when speaking last words; conversation had regenerating effect on Fred
- Watching Mary Garth with evident admiration while she tells Rumpelstiltskin tale

**Rosamond Lydgate (née Vincy)**
- Married to Lydgate; victorious obstinacy never wasting energy
- **Manipulation and Consequences**: Manipulated husband to go riding; accident at Halsell Wood led to loss of baby; regaining brilliant health
- Now possesses knowledge of Casaubon's codicil mentioning Will
- **Response to Debt Crisis**: When Lydgate proposed debt must be paid, fell like mortal chill; when presented with house-selling proposal, went to Mrs. Plymdale with congratulations about coming marriage instead; had secretly disobeyed him by asking father for help; father said more likely to want help himself
- **Business Intervention**: First time thought of doing anything in form of business; felt equal to occasion; called on Mr. Borthrop Trumbull at his office; Trumbull received her with finest manners; revoked Lydgate's order to Trumbull before New Year's Day party
- **Written to Sir Godwin with Refusal**: Had written to Sir Godwin Lydgate requesting aid; awaited answer for nearly three weeks, every day disappointed; Sir Godwin refused all aid; stated wife should not write on business; cannot supply thousand pounds or half that sum; own family drains him; criticized Lydgate for getting through money quickly; suggested he go elsewhere; noted might have gone into army or Church; said he could not help; must consider himself on own legs entirely
- **Response to Lydgate's Confrontation**: When Lydgate spoke of lack of openness and confidence, Rosamond refused to make admissions, claiming she never expressed herself unbecomingly; stated she only wished to prevent him from hurrying into wretchedness without necessity; spoke of hardship of disgrace; expressed wish she had died with baby; her gentleness made words and tears omnipotent; feels aggrieved; does not identify her own acts according to strict classification; has no consciousness her action was false

**Mr. Borthrop Trumbull**
- Auctioneer and man of business; received Rosamond with finest manners at his office
- Good-natured fibre stirred by certainty Lydgate was in difficulties
- Stood before Rosamond with eager solicitude, chiefly benevolent

**Mr. Bulstrode**
- **Recent Development**: Approximately fifteen months after Peter Featherstone's death, became proprietor of Stone Court through Joshua Rigg's land sale
- **Raffles Crisis**: Met Mr. Raffles unexpectedly at Stone Court; Raffles recognized Bulstrode after twenty-five years; offered quarterly annuity; Raffles demanded two hundred pounds to leave immediately, refused regular annuity, departed by three o'clock coach; later appeared wanting twenty-five pounds; declared would come back before long
- **Terror and Helplessness**: Feels helpless; certain that Raffles—unless providence sent death—would come back
- **Past Life**: Young banker's clerk; eminent though young member of Calvinistic dissenting church; happiest time was spiritual conviction and sense of pardon
- **Dunkirk Connection**: Became confidential accountant in Dunkirk's pawnbroker's business; magnificent profit from easy reception of any goods offered without strict inquiry
- **Moral Compromise**: Remembered first moments of shrinking filled with private arguments as prayer; justified business through theological reasoning; perpetual self-justification; soul saturated with belief he did everything for God's sake; yet if could go back in youthful poverty would choose to be missionary
- **Later Years**: Wife died after five years; gradually withdrew capital but did not make sacrifices to end business, carried on for thirteen years before collapsing; became banker, Churchman, public benefactor
- **Current Crisis**: When respectability lasted nearly thirty years, past had risen and immersed his thought
- **Nature of Hypocrisy**: Not coarse hypocrite consciously affecting beliefs; man whose desires stronger than theoretic beliefs, gradually explained gratification into satisfactory agreement with beliefs
- **Repentance and Restitution**: Poured out utterances of repentance; threatening Providence urged propitiation
- **Offer to Will and Reaction**: Wrote letter to Will; met with Will at Shrubs; Will asked if Bulstrode connected with pawnbroker's business where stolen goods received; Bulstrode felt suddenly uncertain; could not tell lie; answered falteringly that Will conjectured rightly; offered five hundred pounds yearly during his life and proportional capital at death; when Will rejected money and departed with determined quickness, Bulstrode suffered violent reaction and wept like woman—first time encountered open expression of scorn from any man higher than Raffles
- **Hypochondriacal Tendency and Medical Consultation**: Recently showing hypochondriacal tendency in his constitution; lack of sleep, really slight exaggeration of habitual dyspeptic symptom, dwelt on as sign of threatening insanity; requested Lydgate call at Bank for consultation; listened eagerly to Lydgate's opinion with sense of comfort
- **Plans for Change—Severe Experience**: Change of plan and shifting of interest stated/betrayed in conversation with Lydgate determined by severe experience since epoch of Mr. Larcher's sale, when Raffles recognized Will Ladislaw and banker had in vain attempted act of restitution which might move Divine Providence to arrest painful consequences; contemplates temporary withdrawal from management of much business, whether benevolent or commercial; thinking of changing residence for a time; probably will close or let 'The Shrubs' and take place near coast under advice as to salubrity; asks Lydgate if that would be measure he would recommend
- **Hospital Plans**: Announced to Lydgate plans to cease personal share in Hospital management; will withdraw support except for having supplied building expenses and contributed large sums to successful working; proposes amalgamation of New Hospital with Infirmary; informed Lydgate that Dorothea may increase contributions and possibly take his place

**Mr. Raffles**
- Known to Bulstrode from twenty-five years prior; addresses him as "Nick"; claims to be visiting stepson Joshua Rigg
- Recalled name was "Ladislaw" and wrote it down in pocket-book; deliberately decided NOT to tell Bulstrode—holds secret knowledge of connection between Bulstrode and Ladislaw, intentionally concealing, treating as card to play
